correctness.rationale: For all N=2M and 1<=k<=N, direct frame-operator calculation yields M independent two-by-two blocks with eigenvalues (k±|C_j|)/2. Moving sums vanish iff the unimodular half-shift correlation is d=gcd(N,k)-periodic and balanced. Odd k gives an odd real-sign period and contradiction. For even k, even M permits alternating binary signs; odd M forces odd h=gcd(M,k/2) and half-period conjugacy. Binary fails, and ternary real-part balance 3u=h is possible iff 3 divides h; otherwise an explicit quadrature construction works. Every admissible correlation is realized by an r-th-root flat window. Checker independently verified 210 realizations, 95 exact spectral endpoint comparisons, and 168 exhaustive small cases. Numeric checks supplement but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: This solves a natural constant-amplitude phase-quantized exact-reconstruction design problem for every even cyclic dimension and every consecutive-mask size. The obstruction at odd k is independent of alphabet size, while binary, ternary and quaternary thresholds change sharply with parity and the divisor 3. It identifies a specific cubic-resonance regime where a smaller digital phase alphabet suffices; a standard block factorization alone does not convey this design boundary. The exact spectrum gives conditioning for all flat candidates, but no unsupported claim of globally optimal nontight conditioning is made.
